S47.prompt: A close-up at night of the post of the old freestanding payphone from reference image 2, on a wet San Francisco Tenderloin sidewalk in the rain. Strapped to the square metal post with grey duct tape is an old black portable cassette tape recorder from the 1990s, plain black plastic with a speaker grille on its lower front, a row of six chunky black mechanical push buttons along its top edge (one of them red), its cassette door hanging open on its hinge with a cassette inside, and a tiny round indicator light on its front, unlit. tenderloin: The street is in San Francisco's Tenderloin: six- and seven-story early-1900s apartment hotels with flat fronts in pale gray, cream and beige painted stucco and terracotta, ornate cornices at the roofline, stacked bay windows, black fire escapes zigzagging down the facades, vertical neon blade signs on the hotels, black scissor security gates and roll-down shutters on the ground-floor shops, a slim gray parking meter, Muni trolley-bus wires strung across the street overhead, and in the distance the street climbs a steep hill.
